items.title: A result nobody can read
items.body: The claimed proof runs to seventeen million lines of machine-checkable code that no mathematician can follow, and its own author says it may be wrong. Medicine will meet the same problem: an answer that is checkable by machine but not understood by any person. For now our rule should hold. If no accountable clinician can explain why a recommendation is right, it is not ready to act on.

items.title: Unverified is unverified
items.body: NLW is careful to call this a historic claim and not a settled fact; some already report errors in the code. Zitron ignores it. Treat it as we would an exciting preprint from a company with a product to sell, announced the week after its flotation: interesting, possibly important, and awaiting independent confirmation.

items.title: Models whose reasoning cannot be seen
items.body: A smaller item matters more for us. New model designs do their reasoning internally and no longer show a trace of it. For clinical safety that removes one of the few ways to audit why a tool said what it said. When a supplier changes model, ask whether the reasoning is still inspectable. Otherwise this edition has little direct clinical relevance.
